title: Offline recursive JSON merge CLI
source_request: Build a usable local Python 3.12 CLI for developers. Given two UTF-8 JSON object files, recursively merge object keys, replace arrays and scalars with the right-hand value, and print the merged object as JSON. Reject invalid JSON and non-object roots with a nonzero exit and useful stderr. Include tests and a README covering setup, usage, tests, and limits. Use no network service or credentials.
requirements: Expose python -m jsonmerge LEFT RIGHT as the command-line entry point.
Read two UTF-8 JSON object files and recursively merge object keys; the right-hand value replaces arrays and scalars.
Print exactly one merged JSON object to stdout on success.
Reject invalid JSON, non-object roots, and missing files with a nonzero exit and useful stderr, without success JSON.
Provide pytest coverage and a README with installation, usage, tests, and limitations.

acceptance_criteria.description: Nested objects merge recursively and right-hand arrays and scalars replace left-hand values.
Invalid JSON, non-object roots, and missing paths fail cleanly.
The package compiles, passes Ruff and pytest, and has usable documentation.

constraints: Use Python 3.12 and the standard library at runtime.
Keep code, tests, and documentation in the supplied repository.
Do not access the network or a hosted service.
assumptions: Input JSON documents fit into memory.
